status_claim: instrumentation / stability / signal-seeking and empirical sizing run. This design CANNOT establish efficacy: 16 S16 episodes cannot separate a modest improvement from sampling variation, and no matched continued-SFT control is run. Report gradient and movement diagnostics, never an efficacy claim.

extension_policy.predeclared: a clean but noisy positive result MAY trigger a balanced 10x8 extension to 20x8 total, keeping 8 episodes per update so the optimization recipe is unchanged and only the optimizer-step count doubles.
extension_policy.pair_reuse: reusing a (task, seed) in a later update is valid -- the policy has changed, so the trajectory is new and on-policy -- but must be declared and balanced: the extension cycles C30 pairs so exposure counts differ by at most one.
extension_policy.sizing: chosen from THIS run's measured gradient norm/variance, policy movement, advantage stability and evaluation variance -- not from external rollout counts, which are not comparable: our correlated multi-turn Tau2 turns are not independent rollouts.
extension_policy.still_exploratory: 20x8 would also be signal-seeking, not confirmatory.

evaluation_note: 16 S16 episodes are weak. Evaluation power should be raised separately -- e.g. all 16 S16 tasks over several fixed seeds -- without touching training or opening F38.

retry_policy.rationale: retrying until eight episodes happen to be format-valid selects lucky trajectories and hides the model's real failure rate. Bounded retries keep the run honest; the failure rate is itself a primary outcome.

format_failures.definition: episode status 'failed' -- a measurement OF THE POLICY
format_failures.unit: SLOT-LEVEL. Only the format-failed episode is resampled; the other seven planned episodes are carried forward unchanged from the refused attempt.
stop_if: >=2 format-failed episodes in ANY single 8-episode attempt
any format failure on the retry attempt (budget exhausted, no exact batch exists)
format_failures.reporting: PRIMARY outcome. Rate is computed over ALL attempted episodes including rejected attempts, and includes the 1/8 observed in pilot_10x8_20260829c update 0.
format_failures.superseded_unit: An earlier draft of this manifest said 'whole batch; never combine successful episodes across attempts'. That is withdrawn as needlessly wasteful: the seven survivors were audited to share one adapter (3869b147ab7ce5d2), one policy version (live-u000), one generation config and require_reasoning=True, and Tau2 episodes are independent of one another. Rerunning them would discard valid paid work and add sampling variation that answers nothing.
why_this_is_still_honest: the refused attempt is preserved unchanged and its format failure counts toward the reported rate
retry_provenance.json in the destination names the retried slot, the attempt number and every carried episode
the carried set must equal the planned roster minus the retried slot -- no shrinking, no foreign ids
source and destination plan hashes must match
only status='failed' may be retried; a 'discarded' episode follows the infrastructure policy and a 'sampled' one is never resampled
events and simulations are FILTERED, so no material from the retried episode survives into the destination
format_failures.bias_note: This is conditional sampling at the SLOT level rather than the batch level. It conditions one planned slot on producing a parseable action, which is a weaker conditioning than resampling the whole batch would be, but it is conditioning nonetheless and keeps the pilot signal-seeking.

infrastructure_failures.definition: episode status 'discarded' -- an environment event, not a policy measurement (e.g. HTTP 408/500)

infrastructure_failures.reporting: separate from format failures; never conflated

expected_cost.note: So ~2 in 3 updates fail the exact-batch gate on the first attempt, and ~41% exhaust the one-retry budget. An earlier draft said ~1 in 3 and ~1 in 9; that was wrong -- it conflated P(>=2 failures)=25% with P(>=1 failure)=64%. This is the real tax of require_reasoning on this SFT lineage and is a measurement, not an obstacle.

retry_policy.declared_conditional_sampling: training batches are conditioned on format validity, so the pilot stays SIGNAL-SEEKING and is not clean efficacy evidence.

code_commit_note: The commit containing the projection/parser/retry implementation this run uses (PROJECTION_VERSION v4, PARSER_VERSION v3, chunk-v2). Earlier drafts pinned f68edfc (pre-fix retry: bulk-copied events, no validations) and edefb83 (lacked the nested-payload event filter). Artifacts produced under either are not this experiment.

interleaved_tool_calls_in_reasoning.what: Qwen sometimes emits <tool_call> blocks INSIDE <think>. The tool JSON is excluded (DeepSeek never sees Hermes serialization), leaving the reasoning discontiguous. A PayloadSpan is one byte range, so that payload is SKIPPED rather than scored.
interleaved_tool_calls_in_reasoning.why_not_fixed_now: Multi-segment support (980e06f) passed every mechanical gate at 94.8% retention and was reverted: it left Hermes markup inside the text sent to DeepSeek as reasoning_content, so the teacher scored later segments conditioned on foreign notation, and _locate's cursor-less find() could map identical segments to the same occurrence. A stub-teacher dry-run cannot detect either. Applying contaminated credit is worse than losing 4.7% of reasoning bytes.
proper_fix_requires: remove tool blocks from the TEACHER's reasoning context, not merely from supervised student indices
define what context each later reasoning segment is scored under
locate segments monotonically by occurrence, never plain find()
bump PROJECTION_VERSION and re-pin the manifest
verify with a non-stub teacher, not only the dry-run
per_update_reporting: number and percentage of affected actions
interleaved_tool_calls_in_reasoning.reframed: This is a MALFORMED GENERATION, not a representation problem for the projector to solve. A real tool call ENDS the assistant action: the environment executes it and a new turn begins. Text emitted after a <tool_call> inside <think> is the model continuing past where it should have stopped -- not a second reasoning segment deserving faithful representation. That is why multi-segment support was the wrong fix: it built machinery to represent something that should not be represented.

long_term_fix.not: more special cases in the projector; each token shape patched individually turns the scorer into a fragile parser maze
structural: enforce the output protocol at generation time -- a tool call ends the action; an embedded one is malformed format, not arbitrary reasoning
parse into an ORDERED semantic representation (ReasoningText | ToolCall | VisibleContent nodes), each keeping its exact byte range and token indices; unknown or ambiguous structures fail closed

render only what DeepSeek supports natively -- if it cannot represent the same ordering without changing context, that region carries no transferred credit; never manufacture adjacency or pass embedded Hermes JSON off as a native tool call
reduce the behaviour through TRAINING: clean examples that close reasoning before a tool call, or a decoding constraint. This addresses why Qwen produces the shape at all

test invariants rather than a growing list of strings: every token supervised or explicitly excluded; supervised bytes identical on both sides; markup zero weight; byte ranges never overlap; locations monotonic and occurrence-specific; ambiguous input fails closed; cache versions change whenever semantics change
long_term_fix.for_this_pilot: v4's conservative skip is correct. The prospective stop rules keep it from silently consuming the run.
